summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC focused on prompt telemetry, PII redaction, and retention settings for VelocitiFin. Key success criteria: <10% latency regression vs baseline, P95 < 450ms for typical prompts, zero PII leakage on redaction test set, and cost within pilot budget. Action items assigned; next step is to run a benchmark harness with 1k-5k representative prompts and iterate redaction rules.
topics: workload sizing (qps, tokens per request, concurrency)
questions: Do you need full prompt retention for audit, or redacted-only?
Will VelocitiFin require on-prem/private deployment for this pilot?
What false-positive tolerance for redaction is acceptable?
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-02-18 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~52 mins
- Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Valdez (Redwood SE), Dana Li (VelocitiFin Head of Data), Priya Nair (ML Lead), Omar Sayed (SecOps), Rafiq Ahmed (Product)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Kickoff for POC to validate prompt-level telemetry and enforce PII redaction + retention controls. Discussed workloads, benchmark metrics, redaction approaches, KMS, and next steps.

00:00 Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Avery from Redwood, and Marco our SE is here. quick agenda — align on success criteria, get the workload sizing, decide what we measure in the benchmark, and cover redaction/retention constraints.
00:22 Dana Li: Hi thanks, jump right in — we run VelocitiFin's customer-sentiment assistant and a trade-alert summarizer. Key ask: we cannot persist raw PII in prompts and also need a proof we won't leak it during the model responses. The POC is mainly to validate our pipeline and that Redwood's hosted offering can hit our latency targets while respecting our data rules.
00:45 Marco Valdez: Got it. Can you give ballpark traffic? qps, average tokens?
00:52 Priya Nair: For the assistant flow, peak is about 12 qps, average 5 qps. Typical prompt size is 180 tokens, responses average 220 tokens. For the trade summarizer it's 2 qps, but longer context up to 1,200 tokens.
01:10 Marco Valdez: Great — that helps. For the POC we usually run scaled-down benchmarks: single-region hosted vs dedicated-capacity sim, target concurrency settings that match 60% of peak to find SLOs. We should capture p50/p95/p99 latency for request end-to-end, cost per million tokens, and correctness metrics for your redaction tests.
01:34 Dana Li: Success criteria — we need p95 < 450ms on the assistant path, p95 < 1.2s on the long-context summarizer, and redaction should remove any 10 types we define with false-negative rate < 0.1% on our labelled test set. Also retention policy — we want 30 days of redacted prompts for debug, and raw prompt retention must be zero unless we run a special approved audit path.
02:05 Marco Valdez: Clarifying: when you say "redacted prompts for debug" do you mean fully redacted copies or tokenized fingerprints/embeddings?
02:13 Priya Nair: Prefer redacted text plus salted hash of original for traceability. Embeddings stored only if they are one-way hashed, we don't want plain-text vectors that could be reverse engineered.
02:26 Omar Sayed: From SecOps, KMS is mandatory. Keys must be customer-managed and rotated on our cadence. Also need to confirm VPC peering or private link; some endpoints can't be public.
02:40 Avery Chen: That's fine, we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments, and for Hosted we have Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) patterns — we'll share the KMS integration notes. Private deployment would be more involved for the POC; do you have timeline pressure?
02:58 Dana Li: We have a compliance review in 8 weeks and want results in 4 weeks to feed that. So pilot needs to be 3-4 weeks of run time, plus a week for analysis. Hosted pilot is preferred if it meets the security checklist, otherwise Dedicated/Private.
03:20 Marco Valdez: For the benchmark harness — we'll want 1k to 5k representative prompts. Priya, can you supply a 1k sample with labels: high-sensitivity flags, expected redacted output, and correctness labels?
03:35 Priya Nair: Yes, we'll provide 1k sample and then a larger 5k set if needed. We'll also include the labelled redaction ground-truth.
03:44 Rafiq Ahmed: A couple of tradeoffs: more aggressive redaction reduces debugability and might increase false positives which annoy product. We'll need to set acceptable thresholds.
03:58 Marco Valdez: For redaction approaches we typically test two options: client-side pre-redaction (regex + ML classifier) before sending, and server-side post-response redaction using Redwood's built-in PII redactor. Each has pros/cons: pre-redaction reduces leakage risk but may increase latency if done synchronously; server-side is simpler but requires trust in our pipeline and careful audit logs.
04:25 Dana Li: Our preference is to avoid sending raw PII anywhere, so pre-redaction is favored. But we need to balance that with not scrubbing useful context like account IDs that are needed for accuracy.
04:40 Marco Valdez: Understood. For pre-redaction we can run a lightweight classifier in your stack (we can provide a containerized shim), and then for validation we run redaction tests server-side on a copy in the POC environment with strict access controls.
04:58 Omar Sayed: Regarding logs: we want request metadata and non-sensitive telemetry (latency, tokens) in logs; request/response bodies only when redacted and kept for 30 days. Audit logs must be tamper-evident. Do you provide WORM or signed audit logs?
05:18 Avery Chen: We have an append-only audit trail that can be forwarded to your SIEM; for Private deployments we support signed log digests. We'll include architecture notes.
05:30 Priya Nair: Another question — embeddings. We use embedding for vector search across customer notes. We do not want raw prompts in embeddings stores. So we need embeddings to be computed in an ephemeral environment or as one-way hashed vectors.
05:47 Marco Valdez: We can scope embeddings as ephemeral (not stored) for pilot, or stored encrypted with KMS keys you control. We'll note both options for the benchmark.
06:05 Dana Li: On success criteria accuracy wise — beyond redaction, we need the assistant to maintain answer quality. We will run 500 QA prompts and expect at least 92% semantic-fidelity pass rate (per your eval harness comparing gold answers).
06:25 Marco Valdez: We'll integrate your eval script into our harness to produce an automated QA metric. Good to lock that down ahead of the run.
06:34 Avery Chen: Ok let's talk timelines and the benchmark run plan. Week 0: share artifacts and tickets, week 1: deploy harness + run initial smoke tests, week 2: full 24-48 hour soak, week 3: analysis and tuning, week 4: final report and remediation steps. Sound right?
06:55 Priya Nair: Yes that timeline matches our compliance review target.
07:02 Marco Valdez: For workload sizing during the harness we'll emulate burst patterns — short spikes to 12qps for the assistant and sustained 2 qps with long context. We'll also test with batching enabled vs disabled to show cost/latency tradeoffs.
07:22 Dana Li: About batching — we need to ensure it doesn't mix customer contexts, so batch boundaries must be per-customer or per-tenant. Can't have cross-tenant batching for VelocitiFin.
07:35 Marco Valdez: Absolutely — we have tenant-aware batching and will configure that for the pilot.
07:41 Rafiq Ahmed: Pricing — can you provide rough numbers for a 4-week pilot with hosted vs dedicated? We need ballpark to get internal sign-off.
07:51 Avery Chen: We'll send scoped pricing. Ballpark: hosted pilot for your projected token volume is likely X — we'll provide exact after we see the 1k sample tokenization. Dedicated has a monthly commit but gives better predictable latency. We'll follow up with a formal estimate.
08:10 Omar Sayed: Legal and compliance will want the security questionnaire and SOC 2 report. Please attach the redaction capabilities and retention controls in the security pack.
08:20 Avery Chen: Will do — action item for us.
08:24 Dana Li: One technical edge case: we sometimes have embedded PDFs and doctext with PII. How does the POC handle attachments?
08:33 Marco Valdez: We can add a preprocessing step to extract text and run the same PII classifier before it hits the model. We'll include that in the harness discussion.
08:43 Priya Nair: For the redaction evaluation — if the classifier flags ambiguous tokens, we want them surfaced to a human-in-loop UI not automatically passed. For pilot we'll test both auto-redact and human-approved modes.
08:58 Marco Valdez: Noted. We'll configure two runs: auto-redact and human-in-loop, and capture FP/FN rates and the latency overhead of human verification.
09:10 Avery Chen: Any other blockers from your side?
09:14 Omar Sayed: Need confirmation on network/VPC options and whether SSH access is required for agents. I'll list required network egress/ingress rules in the action items.
09:22 Dana Li: We'll also provide the labelled redaction dataset and gold answers for the QA eval.
09:28 Avery Chen: Great. Recap of next steps: Redwood to send redaction matrix, KMS notes, SOC2 and security pack, and benchmark harness repo. VelocitiFin to share 1k prompt sample + labels, define the 10 PII types to test, and confirm KMS/network constraints. We'll schedule the benchmark run w/c 2026-02-23.
09:50 Priya Nair: Sounds good.
10:00 Marco Valdez: I'll follow up with a link to the harness and a short runbook for the two redaction modes.
10:10 Avery Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and a proposed schedule.

End of call.

References to shared artifacts: "Redaction options doc" (link: https://redwood.internal/docs/redaction-matrix) — note: link is internal placeholder; "benchmark harness repo" (link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-harness) — sample load script will be shared.

- Redwood: Share redaction options doc + SOC2 and KMS integration notes (Avery)
- Redwood: Provide benchmark harness repo and sample load script (Marco)
- VelocitiFin: Provide 1k labeled prompt set and PII type list (Priya)

Outcome: Agreed pilot scope and timeline; plan to run benchmark w/c 2026-02-23 and deliver final POC report by w/c 2026-03-23.
